tip: ar gael is a set phrase meaning available, built from cael (to get): Mae e-lyfrau ar gael, e-books are available.
Linking yn softens the adjective: mwy becomes fwy. yn fwy plus an adjective means more, as in fwy defnyddiol.
cytuno takes â for with, never gyda: cytuno â'r athro, agree with the teacher.
tuag at means towards and softens what follows: dyrchafiad becomes ddyrchafiad.
Dylai means should: Dylai mwy o bobl ddysgu Cymraeg, more people should learn Welsh.
Llai is the irregular word for less, from bach (small). It never takes an -ach ending.
Negate the present with Dyw...ddim: Dyw hi ddim yn gallu, she can't.
paid â plus a verb-noun tells one person not to do something: paid â stopio, don't stop.
Po fwyaf...po fwyaf frames the more...the more: Po fwyaf dw i'n dysgu, the more I learn.
fy, my, nasal-mutates the next word: tad-cu turns into fy nhad-cu (t to nh).
na, than, aspirate-mutates c, p and t: cyfoeth becomes na chyfoeth.
Better is the irregular gwell, not mwy da: yn well na'r llynedd, better than last year.
Higher is the irregular uwch, from uchel: yn uwch na'r bryn, higher than the hill.
i, to, softens place names: Caerfyrddin becomes i Gaerfyrddin (c to g).
A feminine noun softens the adjective after it: gêm plus cyfartal gives gêm gyfartal.
o, meaning of or from, softens the next word: gwledydd becomes o wledydd.
In Wales is yng Nghymru: yn shifts to yng and Cymru nasal-mutates to Nghymru.
na becomes nag before a vowel: ddyfnach nag oeddwn, deeper than I was.
lle links a place to a clause, meaning where: y fferm lle maen nhw'n gwneud, the farm where they make.
Pe bawn i means if I were: Pe bawn i'n ennill mwy, if I earned more.
Add -af for the most: byr, short, becomes byrraf, shortest, doubling the r.
Adjectives follow the noun in Welsh: band eang gwell reads broadband better, meaning better broadband.
Pe bai sets up an unreal if, answered by byddwn i'n, I would: Pe bai mwy o amser..., byddwn i'n dysgu.
Bad has an irregular superlative: drwg becomes gwaethaf, worst, softened to ffilm waethaf here.
Linking yn softens a following noun too: canwr becomes yn ganwr, a singer (c to g).
Older is the irregular hŷn, from hen: fy mrawd yn hŷn na fi, my brother is older than me.
Three shows gender: tair with feminine nouns, tri with masculine. Here tair ochr, three sides.
For longer adjectives use mwyaf before the word instead of an -af ending: mwyaf poblogaidd, most popular.
Add -ach for -er or more: tawel, quiet, becomes tawelach, softened to dawelach after yn.
sy'n means who or that is, joining a doer to an action: rieni sy'n gweithio, parents who work.
Best is the irregular superlative gorau, from da, never daaf: y gorau, the best.
bod means that after verbs of saying or seeming: Mae'n ymddangos bod pethau'n newid, it seems things change.
A past unreal if adds wedi: Pe bai mwy o adnoddau wedi'u dyrannu, if more had been allocated, not were.
